lessons.title: A button, not a prod change

blocks.heading: A button, not a prod change
blocks.body:
**Edit in Oxygen** is a button in Guides. It opens the topic in desktop Oxygen. Then you check it back in.

An admin turns this on. You do not guess a setting on the live system. The official article is in the Source box. Cloud and on-prem labels differ. Verify.

Keep the DITA version, the catalogs, and the house-style checks the same on the server and on the desktop. If they differ, a topic can look clean in Oxygen and fail when you check it in.

Your lab is to understand the button. It is not to change production.

blocks.heading: Do the work

This lab can fail. Fail when: You paste a made-up config as if you applied it on production.

Expected: Article noted. Setting treated as an admin question. Match-the-server sentence written.

blocks.intro: Walk the steps in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Open the Experience League article Configure Edit in Oxygen (Source box).

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Write oxygen-bootcamp-work/week12/field-log-78.txt: an admin enables the connector. Authors do not guess a setting on production.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Copy the setting name from the pack as a question for an admin (com.adobe.fmdita.xmleditor.config.XmlEditorConfig / xmleditor.editinoxygen=true). Then write ‘verify in the article for your cloud vs on-prem’.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Write: keep DITA version, catalogs, and house-style checks the same on server and desktop.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: Do not paste a made-up config as if you applied it.

blocks.q: Who turns on Edit in Oxygen?
options: Any author, by guessing the setting on production
An admin, after reading the official article
blocks.why: The button is real. The live switch is admin work.

blocks.q: House-style checks differ on the desktop and on the server. What breaks?
options: A topic can look clean in Oxygen and fail when you check it in
blocks.why: Same rules on both desks, or you fight yourself.
